answer.label: Written by
answer.sourceLine: The passage comes from Walt Whitman's Preface to the 1855 Leaves of Grass. It is an extract from a longer sentence; later collected prose prints small variations, including “in school.”

author.name: Walt Whitman
author.heading: About Walt Whitman
author.bio: Walt Whitman repeatedly expanded and revised Leaves of Grass, the poetry collection first issued in 1855. His long, open-ended lines made the individual speaker a meeting place for many voices and experiences.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The Preface gives readers a long sequence of invitations and instructions: how to read, whom to value and how to trust their own judgment. The quoted 1855 passage ↗ follows the re-examination clause by imagining the reader's own flesh becoming a poem.
